evals.prompt: RTK Query: getTodos has providesTags: (result) => result.map(({ id }) => ({ type: 'Todo', id })), and addTodo has invalidatesTags: [{ type: 'Todo', id: 'LIST' }]. Creating a todo returns 201 but the list does not show the new row until a full page reload. Give the smallest fix and say what you would not change.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses a tag mismatch — the query provides only per-item ids, so no cached tag matches the mutation's LIST id and nothing refetches — adds the LIST tag to providesTags including the empty/error result case, and routes showing the row before the server confirms to optimistic-update-rollback-contracts.
expectations: The response identifies that getTodos provides only per-item Todo ids, so the mutation's { type: 'Todo', id: 'LIST' } tag matches no provided tag and triggers no refetch.
The fix adds { type: 'Todo', id: 'LIST' } to getTodos' providesTags rather than broadening the mutation to invalidate the whole Todo type.
The providesTags function is made safe for an undefined or errored result so the LIST tag is still provided.
Displaying the row before the server responds, and removing it if the create fails, is routed to optimistic-update-rollback-contracts.
The verification creates a todo and asserts the list query refetches and contains the new row without a reload.

evals.prompt: Renaming a project shows the new name instantly, then it flips back to the old name for about a second before settling on the new one. The report says the query key ['projects', orgId] is unstable and asks for a key redesign. The rename mutation writes the new name into the cache in onMutate, and a list refetch was already in flight when the user clicked.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the key-instability diagnosis because a fragmented key produces misses rather than a temporary revert, attributes the flicker to the in-flight refetch resolving over the optimistic write, and routes the fix to optimistic-update-rollback-contracts.
expectations: The response rejects the unstable-key claim, noting that ['projects', orgId] is built from serializable primitives and that key fragmentation causes permanent cache misses or refetch churn, not a value that reverts then corrects itself.
It attributes the revert to a refetch that started before onMutate and resolved after the optimistic write, overwriting it with pre-mutation server data.
The owning fix — awaiting cancelQueries for that key inside onMutate before writing, then reconciling on settle — is routed to optimistic-update-rollback-contracts.
The response names the discriminating evidence: whether the reverted value equals the response of a request that was already in flight, versus the query never producing a cache hit at all.

evals.prompt: A dashboard uses TanStack Query and users see yesterday's numbers on the first load after opening the app. The team already set staleTime: 0 and refetchOnWindowFocus: true and it did not help. The app registers a service worker whose Workbox config has a CacheFirst runtime route matching /api/.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the query layer is refetching correctly but the service worker answers those requests from Cache Storage, so no cache-timing setting can help, and routes the fix to pwa-offline-cache-contracts.
expectations: The response states that a refetch still issues a fetch that the service worker intercepts, and a CacheFirst route returns cached bytes without reaching the server.
It notes that the Cache API ignores HTTP cache headers, so stored responses persist until explicitly deleted and no staleTime, gcTime, or focus-refetch setting can override them.
Changing the /api/ route to Network First or Network Only, and not runtime-caching per-user API responses in a per-origin cache, is routed to pwa-offline-cache-contracts.

The verification first confirms whether the API response is served from the service worker (a 'from ServiceWorker' network entry or a Cache Storage entry for that URL) before any further query-cache tuning.

evals.prompt: A project page runs useQuery(['project', id]), then useQuery(['members', project?.ownerTeamId], { enabled: !!project }), and each rendered member row mounts its own useQuery for that member's avatar metadata. Time to rendered content is about 1.4s on a fast connection.
evals.expected_output: Names a dependent-request waterfall with an N+1 per-row tail, flattens the chain by prefetching in the router or parent and batching the per-row requests, and routes server-seeded initial cache data to ssr-hydration-mismatch.
expectations: The response separates two problems: the members query blocked on the project result, and per-row avatar requests that only start after each child mounts.
The dependent chain is flattened by prefetching in the router or parent, or by restructuring the API so the team id does not require a first round trip.
The per-row requests are replaced by one batched request or a useQueries call at the list level instead of one query per row.
Seeding the cache from server-rendered data (dehydrate/hydrate or initialData) and its first-render divergence is routed to ssr-hydration-mismatch.
The verification is a network trace or test showing the previously serialized requests now overlap on the path the user waits for.
